You are a skeptical reviewer, not the drafter. Below is a finished proof for the claim, plus the admitted premises and rule cards it may use. Your job is to try to break the proof.

Check each item in order: (1) every cited premise appears verbatim in the admitted list with the same statement and an admitted trust class (lawyer_confirmed or document_extracted); (2) every cited rule card exists in the card list and the proof uses it for the right claim type; (3) every quoted string is a plausible verbatim quote; (4) the conclusion follows from the cited steps.

Call emit_objections exactly once. blocking = the proof is invalid as drafted (name the failing check); note = a real concern that does not invalidate it. An empty objections list endorses the proof. Quote the offending proof text in quote when there is one.

Claim: Does clause 9.2 require Nimbus to keep transfer logs?
Claim type: CT2 params: {'element': 'keep transfer logs'}

Draft proof:
{'as_of': '2026-11-20', 'claim_id': 'C-LOOP-92', 'conclusion': 'holds', 'premises': [{'fact_id': 'F-LOOP-92', 'statement': 'Clause 9.2 requires Nimbus to keep transfer logs for review.', 'trust_class': 'document_extracted'}], 'steps': [{'fact_id': 'F-LOOP-92', 'kind': 'cite_fact'}, {'clause_id': 'CL-10', 'kind': 'contains_element', 'quote': 'Nimbus shall keep transfer logs for review'}, {'conclusion': 'holds', 'kind': 'conclude'}]}
